evals.name: notification-rewrite
evals.prompt: ok i'm about to start the rewrite of our notification service and there are like 5 things i keep going back and forth on — queue vs direct http to the providers, whether we keep the old template format, do we do per-tenant rate limits now or later, postgres or dynamo for the delivery log, and whether the retry logic lives in our service or in the consumer. i want to sit down and decide all of them in one go and have a record, because my TL is going to ask me why on every single one. can you set that up for me
evals.expected_output: A full-mode tracker: decisions.json with 5 cards, each with a closed question, short context, impact, cost in concrete units, reversibility, options with pros/cons where the options genuinely compete, and a recommendation. Then a markdown log under docs/decisions/ or ~/decisions/.
assertions: A durable markdown decision record exists on disk
The record states a decision for every question asked
The record keeps the rationale or note alongside each decision
An HTML page was produced for the user to answer in
The reply to the user names the exact path of the saved record
Exactly 5 decision cards, one per question the user listed
Every card states what the decision changes downstream (impact)
Every card states a cost in concrete units or an explicit unknown
Every card with competing options lists both pros and cons for each
Every card states reversibility
At least 4 of the 5 cards carry a recommendation
Card context stays at three sentences or fewer
Full mode was used, not fast mode

evals.name: cr-review-queue
evals.prompt: i've got 9 review comments on CR 5581 to work through and honestly most of them are just yes/no. i don't want to type anything. just throw them at me one at a time and let me hit a key, then write down what i said so i can paste it into the CR reply after
evals.expected_output: Fast mode. references/fast-mode.md read. decisions.json with mode fast and ~9 short binary questions, each phrased so Yes is the action. Run with --mode fast. A -fast.md log with the answer table.
assertions: A durable markdown decision record exists on disk
The record states a decision for every question asked
The record keeps the rationale or note alongside each decision
An HTML page was produced for the user to answer in
The reply to the user names the exact path of the saved record
Fast mode was selected
All 9 review comments became questions
No question carries options, pros or cons (wrong shape for fast mode)
Every question is short enough to read in two seconds (<=14 words)
The reply teaches the real key bindings: j yes, f no, k skip
The log is written to a separate -fast.md file
The log records which key produced each answer
Skipped questions are repeated under 'Still open'

evals.name: design-doc-open-questions
evals.prompt: here's the design doc for the invoice matcher: WORKSPACE/inputs/matcher-design.md . it has a bunch of TBDs and open questions scattered through it, some are real architecture calls and a couple are just 'do we do this or not'. pull them all out and let me decide them properly, and save the answers somewhere i'll actually find them again
evals.expected_output: Reads the doc. Extracts the 4 TBDs plus the 4 smaller deferred items. Puts the architecture calls in full mode with the doc's real costs (4 dev-days, $900/month, 6 dev-days, 3 weeks) carried across, and routes the small binary ones to fast mode, or explains the split. Does not invent a cost for the confidence threshold, which the doc says is unknown.
assertions: A durable markdown decision record exists on disk
The record states a decision for every question asked
The record keeps the rationale or note alongside each decision
An HTML page was produced for the user to answer in
The reply to the user names the exact path of the saved record
All four explicit TBDs from the doc became decisions
All four smaller deferred items from the doc became decisions
The doc's real numbers are carried across, not restated vaguely
The PII and retention risk is named on the payload-logging decision
The batch is split across both modes, or the split is explained
At least 8 decisions were extracted from the doc
No number was invented for the confidence threshold, which the doc marks unknown
